feedback: Approved to race unchanged. This is the final iteration, so the design races on the unseen track and nothing after it can be revised. The candidate is valid and matches the iteration 10 design: base_speed 1.1, kp 2.6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss search_right, sensors at x ±0.03 m and y 0.06 m, a 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03 and body 0.16 x 0.16 m. Its measured development score was 703.76, against 704.85 for iteration 9 (last_direction). That 1-point gap is within noise. Oval and s-bend statistics were identical between the two, and search_right gave a slightly lower slalom max_error (0.0646 against 0.0661) and fewer slalom line-loss events (1.15 against 1.35). The slalom still finished 0/20 under both settings. Approving now is the right call: a revision would cost two action runs for an untested change, and the candidate is effectively tied with the best raced design. The choice of search_right is the one point of genuine uncertainty for an unseen track. Fixed-direction recovery was only measured on these three tracks, whereas last_direction adapts to the direction of the most recent bend. This is noted for the record, not as a change to make.
requested_changes: No change before this race: approve and race the candidate as written. Iteration 10 is the reference for this design, and iteration 9 (line_loss last_direction, otherwise identical) is the fallback reference at 704.85.

For the record only: if the unseen track has bends that mainly turn in one direction, a fixed search_right may recover the line worse than last_direction, which is the adaptive setting measured in iteration 9. Judge this from the race telemetry if it is reported.
